messages:
rachel: Quick sync about pin/rollout metadata — idea is to treat pins as two-layer contracts: identity (alias) + provenance (artifact id + lineage). Wanted to surface the sketch before I file a formal RFC.

morgan: Love two-layer idea. What fields are you thinking for provenance?

rachel: Minimal: {artifact: {algo,hash}}, plus optional lineage: previous_artifact refs and `deployed_at` timestamps. We can then decide migration rules based on lineage distance.

sanjay: Lineage is handy. Example: quantize pipeline auto-produces new artifact; lineage shows it came from `sha256:x -> sha256:y` and also includes `transform: q4_0`. UI can then show "derived from" when offering fallback choices.

oliver: We should also bake in a `pin_tier` or `pin_level` concept: "hard-lock" vs "preference" vs "suggested". Current messy: some tenants call things "pinned" when they mean "preferred".

rachel: Agreed. Proposed enum: ["hard","soft","sticky"]. Hard = tenant intent to block incompatibles; soft = prefer match but allow fallback; sticky = temporary override that decays after N uses/time.

nina: Sticky sounds useful for experiments — e.g., canary users get sticky pin then it expires. How to express expiration?

rachel: Add optional `expires_at` + `decay_policy` (how it falls back). For sticky default: expires_at or `max_requests`.

morgan: Migration concern: we have hundreds of legacy pins that only store alias string. We need a safe default if fingerprint missing. Maybe we treat legacy pins as `soft` with `origin=legacy` and schedule auto-fingerprint jobs.

sanjay: Implementation note: resolver should treat artifact fingerprints as authoritative when present. Alias lookup can map to many artifacts; prefer exact fingerprint match first. For soft pins, if no exact match, resolver picks best candidate by compatibility score. Score based on tokenizer, kv-cache-compat, quantization tag.

oliver: Do we want `compatibility_tags` to be free-form strings? We should scope them (prefixes) to avoid explosion. E.g., `t:tok-bpe-v2`, `q:q4_0`, `k:kv-v1`.

nina: Good call. Namespacing avoids collisions and keeps tags short. Also helps index size.

rachel: Example admin JSON (we'll send this only on pin-create/update): ```json
{
  "alias": "redwood/gptx-1",
  "provenance": {
    "artifact": {"algo":"sha256","hash":"e3b0c442..."},
    "derived_from": ["sha256:abc123"],
    "transform_hint": "quantize-q4_0"
  },
  "level": "sticky",
  "origin": "tenant-admin",
  "expires_at": "2026-07-15T12:00:00Z",
  "compat_tags": ["t:tok-bpe-v2","q:q4_0"],
  "meta": {"created_by":"rachel"}
}
```

morgan: Two asks: 1) `meta` should be flat key-values only in admin API; 2) make sure runtime request paths accept `pin_ref` short string to keep inference path small.

rachel: Yep — runtime will only see `pin_ref` most of the time. Admin APIs carry full object. We'll store canonical expanded object server-side.

ops-bot: Note: nightly job `pin-fingerprint-backfill` queued (ticket INFRA-1247).

oliver: Operational concern: if we enforce strict fingerprints, rollout safety could block customers during artifact churn. Need an escape hatch: admin can set `allowed_migrations` list or a temporary `bypass_until` window for infra teams.

sanjay: Maybe allow `migration_mode` per-pin: ["manual","auto-suggest","auto-apply"] with defaults conservative. Auto-apply only for soft pins with matching compatibility score > threshold.

nina: Telemetry: emit `pin_resolution` event with fields: pin_ref, chosen_artifact_hash, fallback_reason (if any), resolution_latency_ms, origin. That helps troubleshooting.

rachel: Agree. Also include `lineage_distance` (number of hops to preferred artifact) in telemetry so we can tune auto-migration heuristics.

morgan: Tests: add unit tests for resolver: exact fingerprint match, alias-only match with multiple artifacts, soft->fallback with score tie-breakers, sticky expiry behavior. Also integration test that simulates quantize pipeline swapping artifact hash.

rachel: Migration steps (brief): 1) DB schema add `provenance` proto column + `pin_level` enum, 2) backfill job attempts to compute fingerprints from model store, 3) mark ambiguous legacy pins as `soft` and notify tenant owner, 4) enable telemetry and compatibility-check API.

oliver: For the compatibility-check API: useful to return ranked candidates and a short human message (e.g., "tokenizer mismatch: tokenizer v1 vs v2"). UI can use that.

sanjay: Security: make sure artifact hash doesn't leak internal storage layout — only publish hash and non-sensitive transform hints.

rachel: Good call. We'll redact any internal S3 paths etc. Only store minimal provenance.

morgan: Sounds actionable. Can you open the RFC PR with schema examples and a migration runbook? I'll pick up resolver prototype and tests.

rachel: Will do. I'll also add a short console mock showing how pinned alias and fingerprint are displayed.

nina: LGTM from me.

sanjay: +1.

ops-bot: CI: `pin-backfill` job created INFRA-1247 — ETA 24h.

rachel: Thanks all — I'll post RFC link when ready. If anyone wants to tweak enums or tag prefixes, speak up here.
